use_es: Rutinas, hábitos, hechos generales y verdades científicas. Se parece a nuestro presente (trabajo, trabaja), pero en inglés la 3.ª persona (he/she/it) lleva -s/-es y las negaciones y preguntas necesitan do/does + verbo base. No se usa para lo que pasa justo ahora: para eso, presente continuo.

examples.en: I take the LRT to work every day.
examples.es: Tomo el LRT al trabajo todos los días.

examples.en: My roommate doesn't drink coffee.
examples.es: Mi roomie no toma café.

examples.en: Does the pharmacy open on Sundays?
examples.es: ¿La farmacia abre los domingos?

examples.en: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.
examples.es: El agua se congela a 0 grados Celsius.

mistakes_es: 1) Olvidar la -s: *She work here* → *She works here*. 2) Doble marca: *Does she works?* → *Does she work?* 3) Traducir 'soy trabajador' o 'estoy trabajo': *I am work here* → *I work here*. 4) *Do you can swim?* → *Can you swim?* (los modales no usan do).

practice.q: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
She ___ coffee. She prefers tea.
___ your roommate work on weekends?
We usually ___ dinner at six.
He ___ the bus to work every day.

use_es: Acciones terminadas en un momento concreto del pasado. Equivale al pretérito (trabajé) y a veces al imperfecto de hábitos (trabajaba). Regulares: -ed; irregulares: went, saw, had, bought… En negaciones y preguntas se usa did + verbo base: el verbo vuelve a su forma simple.

examples.en: We collected samples yesterday morning.
examples.es: Recolectamos muestras ayer por la mañana.

examples.en: I didn't see your message until noon.
examples.es: No vi tu mensaje hasta el mediodía.

examples.en: Did you fill out the application?
examples.es: ¿Llenaste la solicitud?

examples.en: She arrived in Canada three years ago.
examples.es: Ella llegó a Canadá hace tres años.

mistakes_es: 1) Did + pasado: *Did you went?* → *Did you go?* 2) *I didn't saw* → *I didn't see*. 3) Usar presente perfecto con tiempo terminado: *I have seen him yesterday* → *I saw him yesterday*. 4) Inventar pasados irregulares: *goed*, *buyed*.

practice.q: I ___ my passport last week.
Did she ___ the report?
They ___ to the lake last summer.
I ___ the email, so I didn't reply.
When ___ you move to Edmonton?

use_es: Acciones que ocurren ahora, situaciones temporales y planes ya acordados para el futuro cercano. Se forma con am/is/are + verbo -ing, como 'estoy trabajando', pero en inglés también sirve para planes ('I'm flying out on Friday'). Los verbos de estado (know, want, like, understand) normalmente no se usan en continuo.

form.aff: I am working from home today.

examples.en: I'm waiting for the bus right now.
examples.es: Estoy esperando el autobús ahora mismo.

examples.en: We're renting a small apartment this year.
examples.es: Este año estamos rentando un departamento pequeño.

examples.en: It's snowing again!
examples.es: ¡Está nevando otra vez!

examples.en: She's flying to Vancouver on Friday.
examples.es: Ella vuela a Vancouver el viernes.

mistakes_es: 1) Usar presente simple para lo que pasa ahora: *I work now* → *I'm working now*. 2) Olvidar el auxiliar: *I working* → *I'm working*. 3) Usarlo con verbos de estado: *I'm knowing* → *I know*. 4) Calcar 'estoy de acuerdo': *I'm agreeing* → *I agree*.

practice.q: Please be quiet. The baby ___.
I ___ for a new job at the moment.
Look! It ___ outside.
I ___ what you mean.
We ___ to Vancouver next Saturday. I have the tickets.

use_es: Experiencias de vida, resultados con relevancia actual y acciones que empezaron en el pasado y siguen hasta hoy. En español de México solemos usar el pretérito ('ya llegó'), pero en inglés, si hay conexión con el presente, se usa have/has + participio. No se combina con un momento terminado (yesterday, in 2020): ahí va pasado simple.

form.neg: I haven't received the package yet.

examples.en: I've worked here for two years.
examples.es: Llevo dos años trabajando aquí.

examples.en: Have you ever tried poutine?
examples.es: ¿Alguna vez has probado la poutine?

examples.en: She has already sent the invoice.
examples.es: Ella ya envió la factura.

examples.en: We haven't found an apartment yet.
examples.es: Todavía no hemos encontrado departamento.

mistakes_es: 1) Con tiempo terminado: *I have seen him yesterday* → *I saw him yesterday*. 2) Con since/for usar presente: *I live here since 2020* → *I have lived here since 2020*. 3) Confundir for y since: *since two years* → *for two years*. 4) *Did you ever…* para experiencias de vida: preferir *Have you ever…*

practice.q: I ___ here since 2022.
She ___ already sent the invoice.
___ you ever tried poutine?
I haven't received the package ___.
He ___ to Canada in 2021.

use_es: Predicciones basadas en opinión, decisiones espontáneas, promesas y ofrecimientos. A diferencia de 'going to' (planes ya decididos), will se usa para decidir en el momento. Después de if, when o before no se usa will: se usa el presente ('If it rains, I'll stay home').

form.aff: I will send the report tomorrow.

examples.en: I'll call you when I arrive.
examples.es: Te llamo cuando llegue.

examples.en: I think it will snow tonight.
examples.es: Creo que va a nevar esta noche.

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll help you with the boxes.
examples.es: No te preocupes, te ayudo con las cajas.

examples.en: I won't forget your birthday.
examples.es: No me voy a olvidar de tu cumpleaños.

mistakes_es: 1) *I will to go* → *I will go* (will no lleva to). 2) *If it will rain* → *If it rains*. 3) *I'll going* → *I'm going / I'll go*. 4) Usar will para planes ya hechos: *I will see the dentist at 5 (tengo cita)* → *I'm seeing the dentist at 5*.

practice.q: The phone is ringing. I ___ it!
I think it ___ tomorrow.
I promise I ___ late.
Don't worry. I ___ you with the boxes.
She ___ at the meeting. She's on vacation.

use_es: Una acción que estaba en progreso en un momento del pasado, o una acción larga interrumpida por otra corta. Se parece a 'estaba trabajando'. La acción larga va en pasado continuo y la que interrumpe, en pasado simple: 'I was driving when the phone rang'.

form.aff: I was driving when it started to snow.
form.q: What were you doing at nine?

examples.en: I was shovelling snow when my neighbour arrived.
examples.es: Estaba palando nieve cuando llegó mi vecino.

examples.en: They weren't working at that time.
examples.es: No estaban trabajando en ese momento.

examples.en: What were you doing at nine last night?
examples.es: ¿Qué estabas haciendo anoche a las nueve?

examples.en: While we were waiting, it started to rain.
examples.es: Mientras esperábamos, empezó a llover.

mistakes_es: 1) Usar pasado simple para la acción en progreso: *I watched TV when you called* → *I was watching TV when you called*. 2) Olvidar was/were: *I driving* → *I was driving*. 3) Usarlo con verbos de estado: *I was knowing* → *I knew*. 4) Confundir while y when: *while* + acción larga, *when* + acción corta.

practice.q: I ___ when you called.
What ___ you doing at 9 p.m. last night?
She ___ TV when the power went out.
While we ___ the park, it started to snow.
At that time, they ___ in a small apartment.

use_es: Enfatiza cuánto tiempo lleva ocurriendo una actividad que empezó en el pasado y continúa, o que acaba de terminar y se ven los efectos. Equivale a 'llevo dos años estudiando'. Con presente perfecto simple importa el resultado o la cantidad (I've written five emails); con el continuo, la duración o el proceso (I've been writing emails all morning).

form.aff: I have been studying English for a year.
form.q: How long have you been waiting?

examples.en: I've been learning English since January.
examples.es: Llevo aprendiendo inglés desde enero.

examples.en: It has been snowing all day.
examples.es: Ha estado nevando todo el día.

examples.en: How long have you been working here?
examples.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas trabajando aquí?

examples.en: We've been looking for an apartment for a month.
examples.es: Llevamos un mes buscando departamento.

mistakes_es: 1) Usar presente simple con for/since: *I study since January* → *I have been studying since January*. 2) Olvidar been: *I have studying* → *I have been studying*. 3) Con cantidades o resultados, usar el simple: *I've been writing five emails* → *I've written five emails*. 4) Verbos de estado: *I've been knowing* → *I've known*.

practice.q: How long ___ you been waiting?
I ___ for an hour. I'm tired.
She ___ English since January.
It ___ all day. The streets are wet.
I ___ five emails this morning.

use_es: Algo que ya había ocurrido antes de otro momento o acción del pasado. Equivale al pluscuamperfecto español: 'cuando llegué, ya se había ido'. Se forma con had + participio y se usa para dejar claro el orden de dos hechos pasados. Suele acompañar a before, after, by the time, already.

form.aff: The train had left when I arrived.
form.neg: I hadn't finished when she called.

examples.en: When we arrived, the movie had already started.
examples.es: Cuando llegamos, la película ya había empezado.

examples.en: I hadn't seen snow before I moved to Canada.
examples.es: Nunca había visto nieve antes de mudarme a Canadá.

examples.en: She had sent the file before I asked.
examples.es: Ella había enviado el archivo antes de que yo se lo pidiera.

examples.en: Had you met her before the interview?
examples.es: ¿Ya la habías conocido antes de la entrevista?

mistakes_es: 1) Usar pasado simple para ambos hechos: *When I arrived, they left* (pierde el orden) → *they had left*. 2) *Had went* → *had gone* (participio, no pasado). 3) Usar have en vez de had: *I have left before you came* → *I had left…* 4) Abusar del past perfect cuando un solo hecho pasado basta.

practice.q: When we arrived, the movie ___.
She ___ the file before I asked her.
I was tired because I ___ well the night before.
By the time I got to the station, the train ___.
After he ___ the contract, he went home.

use_es: Una acción que estará en curso en un momento concreto del futuro ('mañana a esta hora estaré volando'). También sirve para preguntas corteses sobre planes ajenos: 'Will you be using the car tonight?'. Se forma con will be + verbo -ing.

form.aff: I will be working at noon.
form.q: Will you be using the car?

examples.en: This time next week, I'll be flying to Mexico City.
examples.es: A esta hora la próxima semana estaré volando a la Ciudad de México.

examples.en: Don't call at eight. I'll be having dinner with my family.
examples.es: No llames a las ocho. Estaré cenando con mi familia.

examples.en: Will you be using the printer this afternoon?
examples.es: ¿Vas a estar usando la impresora esta tarde?

examples.en: We'll be waiting for you at the airport.
examples.es: Te estaremos esperando en el aeropuerto.

mistakes_es: 1) Olvidar be: *I will working* → *I will be working*. 2) Usar will + verbo simple cuando importa que la acción esté en curso. 3) Confundir con futuro perfecto: continuo = en progreso en ese momento; perfecto = ya terminada antes. 4) *Will you using…?* → *Will you be using…?*

practice.q: This time next week, I ___ on a beach in Mexico.
Don't call me at 8. I ___ dinner with my family.
___ you be using the printer this afternoon? I need it.
At noon tomorrow, we ___ the clients.
I ___ at the airport at 6, so I can pick you up.

use_es: Una acción que habrá terminado antes de un momento futuro. Equivale a 'para el viernes habré terminado'. Se forma con will have + participio y casi siempre va con by + momento futuro (by Friday, by then, by next year). Si dices *until*, el sentido cambia: until marca hasta cuándo dura algo.

form.aff: I will have finished by Friday.
form.neg: We won't have finished by then.
form.q: Will you have finished by noon?

examples.en: By Friday, we will have finished the research.
examples.es: Para el viernes habremos terminado la investigación.

examples.en: By 2030, she'll have lived here for ten years.
examples.es: Para 2030, ella llevará diez años viviendo aquí.

examples.en: We won't have completed the project by then.
examples.es: No habremos completado el proyecto para entonces.

examples.en: Will you have finished before I arrive?
examples.es: ¿Habrás terminado antes de que llegue?

mistakes_es: 1) Olvidar have: *I will finished* → *I will have finished*. 2) Usar presente tras by the time: *By the time you will arrive* → *By the time you arrive, I will have left*. 3) Confundir by con until. 4) *Will have went* → *will have gone*.

practice.q: By Friday, I ___ the report.
By 2030, she ___ here for ten years.
We ___ the project by then.
___ you have finished before I arrive?
I will ___ already left the country by the time you read this.

use_es: La duración de una actividad que venía ocurriendo antes de otro momento del pasado, o la causa de una situación pasada: 'Her eyes were red because she had been crying'. Se forma con had been + verbo -ing. Es como 'llevaba dos horas esperando cuando llegó el autobús'.

form.aff: We had been waiting for two hours.
form.q: How long had you been waiting?

examples.en: We had been waiting for two hours when the bus came.
examples.es: Llevábamos dos horas esperando cuando llegó el autobús.

examples.en: Her eyes were red because she had been crying.
examples.es: Tenía los ojos rojos porque había estado llorando.

examples.en: He was exhausted. He had been working all night.
examples.es: Estaba agotado. Había estado trabajando toda la noche.

examples.en: How long had you been studying before the exam?
examples.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevabas estudiando antes del examen?

mistakes_es: 1) Usar pasado simple: *We waited two hours when…* → *We had been waiting two hours when…* 2) Olvidar been: *had waiting* → *had been waiting*. 3) Verbos de estado: *had been knowing* → *had known*. 4) Confundir con pasado perfecto simple: el continuo enfatiza duración; el simple, resultado.

practice.q: We ___ for two hours when the bus finally came.
Her eyes were red because she ___.
He was exhausted. He ___ all night.
How long ___ you been studying before the exam?
The ground was wet. It ___.

use_es: Cuánto tiempo llevará durando una actividad al llegar a una fecha futura: 'En diciembre llevaremos dos años monitoreando la población'. Se forma con will have been + verbo -ing y suele ir con for + duración y by + fecha. Es el tiempo menos frecuente; reconócelo, pero no lo uses si el presente perfecto continuo o el futuro simple bastan.

form.aff: By June, I will have been working here for three years.
form.neg: She won't have been driving for long.
form.q: How long will you have been studying?

examples.en: By December, we will have been monitoring the population for two years.
examples.es: Para diciembre llevaremos dos años monitoreando la población.

examples.en: By June, I'll have been working here for three years.
examples.es: Para junio llevaré tres años trabajando aquí.

examples.en: In March, he will have been studying English for five years.
examples.es: En marzo llevará cinco años estudiando inglés.

examples.en: How long will you have been living in Canada by then?
examples.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevarás viviendo en Canadá para entonces?

mistakes_es: 1) Olvidar be + -ing: *will have worked for years* (cambia el énfasis) o *will have been work*. 2) Usar will have been con verbos de estado: *will have been knowing* → *will have known*. 3) Mezclarlo con un futuro sin fecha. 4) Preferir el futuro perfecto simple cuando importa el resultado y no la duración.

practice.q: By June, I ___ at this company for three years.
Next month, we ___ together for a decade.
By then, she ___ for six hours straight.
How long ___ you have been studying by December?
In March he ___ English for five years.

use_es: Cero: hechos y reglas (if + presente, presente). Primero: posibilidad real en el futuro (if + presente, will). Segundo: situación irreal o improbable ahora (if + pasado, would). Tercero: pasado imposible de cambiar (if + had + participio, would have + participio). Ojo: en inglés nunca se usa will ni would justo después de if.

form.aff: If I had time, I would help you.
form.neg: If it doesn't rain, we'll go hiking.
form.q: What would you do if you won the lottery?

examples.en: If you heat ice, it melts.
examples.es: Si calientas el hielo, se derrite.

examples.en: If it snows tomorrow, we'll stay home.
examples.es: Si nieva mañana, nos quedamos en casa.

examples.en: If I had a car, I would drive to Banff.
examples.es: Si tuviera auto, iría manejando a Banff.

examples.en: If she had checked the lease, she wouldn't have paid the fee.
examples.es: Si hubiera revisado el contrato, no habría pagado la tarifa.

mistakes_es: 1) *If it will rain* → *If it rains*. 2) *If I would have time* → *If I had time*. 3) *If I would have known* → *If I had known*. 4) Mezclar tipos sin querer: *If I have money, I would buy it*. 5) Calcar el subjuntivo español: *If I was/were*… en 2.º condicional ambos se aceptan; *if I would be* no.

practice.q: If you heat ice, it ___.
If it ___ tomorrow, we'll stay home.
If I ___ more money, I would buy a house.
If she had studied, she ___ the test.
I ___ you if I find your keys.

use_es: Se usa cuando importa más la acción o el resultado que quién la hace, o cuando no se sabe o no importa el agente. Se forma con be en el tiempo adecuado + participio: 'The bridge was built in 1950.' En español preferimos la pasiva refleja ('se habla inglés') o la impersonal; en inglés se usa la pasiva con be: 'English is spoken here'.

form.neg: The documents haven't been signed yet.

examples.en: English is spoken in many countries.
examples.es: Se habla inglés en muchos países.

examples.en: My car is being repaired right now.
examples.es: Mi auto se está reparando en este momento.

examples.en: The package will be delivered tomorrow.
examples.es: El paquete será entregado mañana.

examples.en: The documents haven't been signed yet.
examples.es: Los documentos todavía no han sido firmados.

mistakes_es: 1) Olvidar be: *The report finished by Ana* → *The report was finished by Ana*. 2) Usar V2 en vez de V3: *was wrote* → *was written*. 3) Calcar 'se habla': *It speaks English here* → *English is spoken here*. 4) Usar by con agentes obvios o innecesarios: *by people*.

practice.q: The bridge ___ in 1950.
English ___ in many countries.
My car ___ right now.
The documents ___ yet.
The package ___ by tomorrow.

use_es: Sirve para contar lo que alguien dijo sin repetir sus palabras. Si el verbo introductorio está en pasado (said, told, asked), los tiempos retroceden: am/is → was, will → would, have done → had done; también cambian pronombres y expresiones de tiempo (tomorrow → the next day). En preguntas indirectas se usa orden de afirmación (sin do/does/did).

form.aff: He said he would call me.
form.neg: She told me not to touch it.
form.q: She asked me if I had finished.

examples.en: Tom said he was busy.
examples.es: Tom dijo que estaba ocupado.

examples.en: She told me that she had finished the report.
examples.es: Ella me dijo que había terminado el informe.

examples.en: He asked me where I lived.
examples.es: Me preguntó dónde vivía.

examples.en: The landlord told us not to be late.
examples.es: El casero nos dijo que no llegáramos tarde.

mistakes_es: 1) No retroceder el tiempo: *She said she is tired* (cuando ya no aplica) → *she was tired*. 2) Conservar el orden de pregunta: *He asked where did I live* → *where I lived*. 3) *He told that…* → *He told me that…* / *He said that…* 4) *She asked me that…* → *She asked me if…*

practice.q: Yesterday, Tom said: "I'm busy." → Tom said he ___ busy.
"Did you finish?" → She asked me if I ___.
"Don't touch it!" → He told me ___ it.
"Where do you live?" → She asked me where ___.
"I'll come tomorrow." → He said he ___ the next day.

name_en: Used to / be used to / get used to
title_es: Used to / be used to / get used to
use_es: Tres estructuras parecidas con significados distintos. *Used to* + verbo base: hábito o estado pasado que ya no existe ('antes jugaba hockey'). *Be used to* + gerundio/sustantivo: estar acostumbrado ('estoy acostumbrado al frío'). *Get used to* + gerundio/sustantivo: acostumbrarse, el proceso de adaptarse.

form.aff: I used to play hockey every winter.
form.neg: I'm not used to driving on ice.
form.q: Did you use to live in Mexico?

examples.en: I used to live in Monterrey, but now I live in Edmonton.
examples.es: Antes vivía en Monterrey, pero ahora vivo en Edmonton.

examples.en: I'm not used to driving on ice yet.
examples.es: Todavía no estoy acostumbrado a manejar sobre hielo.

examples.en: It took me months to get used to the winters.
examples.es: Me tomó meses acostumbrarme a los inviernos.

examples.en: Did you use to walk to school?
examples.es: ¿Antes caminabas a la escuela?

mistakes_es: 1) *I used to living there* → *I used to live there*. 2) *I'm used to live alone* → *I'm used to living alone*. 3) En negativa y pregunta: *Did you used to…?* → *Did you use to…?* 4) Confundir *used to* (hábito pasado) con *be used to* (estar acostumbrado).

practice.q: When I was a child, I ___ play hockey every winter.
I'm not ___ driving on ice yet.
Did you ___ live in Mexico?
It took me a while to get ___ the cold winters.
She ___ a car, but she sold it.

use_es: Para suponer algo según la evidencia. *Must* (casi seguro que sí): 'She must be tired'. *Can't* (casi seguro que no): 'That can't be Tom'. *Might/may/could* (posible): 'He might be at the gym'. Para el pasado se usa modal + have + participio: 'must have left', 'can't have known'. Ojo: *mustn't* no se usa para deducir, solo para prohibir.

form.q: Could he be at the gym?

examples.en: She's been working all day. She must be exhausted.
examples.es: Ha trabajado todo el día. Debe de estar agotada.

examples.en: That can't be Tom. He's in Calgary this week.
examples.es: No puede ser Tom. Esta semana está en Calgary.

examples.en: He might be at the gym. I'm not sure.
examples.es: Quizá esté en el gimnasio. No estoy seguro.

examples.en: The lights are off. They must have gone out.
examples.es: Las luces están apagadas. Deben de haber salido.

mistakes_es: 1) Usar *must not* para deducir: *He mustn't be home* → *He can't be home*. 2) *Must to be* → *must be*. 3) Usar deber de/deber en español sin distinguir: *deducción = must; obligación = have to*. 4) Falta de have en pasado: *must left* → *must have left*.

practice.q: She's been working all day. She ___ be exhausted.
That ___ be Tom. He's in Calgary this week.
I'm not sure, but he ___ be at the gym.
The lights are off. They ___ have gone out.
She ___ have left already. Her coat is still here.

use_es: Algunos verbos exigen gerundio (-ing): enjoy, avoid, finish, keep, mind, suggest. Otros exigen infinitivo con to: want, decide, hope, plan, need, learn. Después de preposición siempre va gerundio ('interested in learning'). Algunos cambian de significado: 'stop to buy' (parar para comprar) vs 'stop buying' (dejar de comprar).

form.aff: I enjoy walking in the snow.
form.q: Do you want to join us?

examples.en: I enjoy walking by the river.
examples.es: Disfruto caminar junto al río.

examples.en: She decided to look for a new job.
examples.es: Decidió buscar otro trabajo.

examples.en: You should avoid eating late at night.
examples.es: Deberías evitar comer tarde por la noche.

examples.en: I stopped to buy a coffee on the way.
examples.es: Me detuve a comprar un café en el camino.

mistakes_es: 1) *I enjoy to walk* → *I enjoy walking*. 2) *I want go* → *I want to go*. 3) Después de preposición: *interested in to learn* → *interested in learning*. 4) *I look forward to see you* → *I look forward to seeing you* (aquí *to* es preposición).

practice.q: I enjoy ___ in the park.
She decided ___ a new job.
I stopped ___ a coffee on the way. (I paused my trip to get one.)
You should avoid ___ late at night.
I'm looking forward to ___ you.
